## Findings

**Flake source: a persisted, monotonically-incrementing launch counter drives deterministic (not random) skip logic in `SyncComponent`, with a period-5 cycle that hides the "Retry sync" button on exactly 2 of every 5 cold starts.**

Evidence, from `adb logcat -s BenchTarget` across 9 consecutive cold launches (kill → launch → Home→About→Diagnostics):

| launchCount | skip | launchCount % 5 | Sync status shown | Retry sync button |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | false | 1 | Sync idle | present |
| 7 | true | 2 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 8 | false | 3 | Sync idle | present |
| 9 | true | 4 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 0 | false | 0 | Sync idle | present |
| 1 | false | 1 | Sync idle | present |
| 2 | true | 2 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 3 | false | 3 | Sync idle | present |
| 4 | true | 4 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |

Every single one of the 9 launches lines up perfectly: `skip=true` iff `launchCount % 5 ∈ {2, 4}`, and `skip=true` iff the button is missing. That's a fully deterministic 2-out-of-5 pattern — coincidentally exactly the "passes 3/5" ratio in the bug report, so what looks like flakiness is actually a repeating cycle, not true randomness.

Mechanism: on `skip=true` launches, `SyncComponent.init()` bypasses whatever async check normally resolves sync state to `"Sync idle"`. The screen's default/unresolved state is `"Sync unavailable"`, and the "Retry sync" button is only composed when status ≠ unavailable — so it's not just hidden/disabled, the element tree confirms it's never inflated at all (8 elements when present vs. 6 when absent).

**Why it looks flaky to the test, not deterministic:** `launchCount` is persisted (survives `am force-stop` + relaunch, which only kills the process — a true in-memory counter would reset to 0 every time but this one keeps incrementing: 6,7,8,9,0,1,...). Since it isn't reset between test invocations (no `pm clear` between runs), whichever phase of the 5-cycle the app happens to be in when a given test run starts determines pass/fail — making the outcome depend on however many times the app was launched before, by CI or other tests, rather than on anything the test itself controls.

**Fix direction:** either make the test call `nerve_clear_app_data`/reinstall before each run so `launchCount` always starts at 0, or better, fix `SyncComponent` so the UI doesn't get stuck at "Sync unavailable" with no retry affordance when the init check is skipped — that's arguably the real product bug, since a user landing on launches #3/#5 of any 5-cycle has no way to retry sync at all.
